### 2026-10-17: # Outer Frame Done!

**5h**

# Outer Frame Done!

## tldr

Today, I finished the CAD for the outer frame of save my thinkpad. This features holes for screws, a v-rail and spaces for hinges. I based my measurements of a Lenovo L13 2-in-1 Gen 5.

## timeline

I started with sketching, which was very time consuming as I had to plan out and measure with my capilers. if anything goes wrong here or if I do not plan ahead, the whole CAD model is useless.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/0f2e878c43871c6878459577c99e8150bcd71606f89c5201d7fbb27b4ade7cd4.png)

Afterwards, I started work extruding!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/95d625f89b760c2e29e0a3343bdf3a554dcfee108524af816f026b640976f5e7.png)

This is where things get tricky. The V-rail was a STEP model off the web, and I had to mesh it to convert to body. I am running fusion on a (pretty crusty) computer meaning this took FOREVER.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/a6b9518737d56fc14a44c249ab9d80273cbc5df3d2cdedc8af5e7ebc0ce69827.png)

Afterwards, I got to work putting this into the frame.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/046303323ac1957c6d19c1ee1fff9104d0648ecafab23d1b6a2103e899b9536f.png)

Finally, I added holes. This was fun. This was easy. This was also boring as-

I got the modelling done after a while.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/1da65f2f9ae78b39cc07f84557d624e4e153016c3ef9a8becafd08fa1b603c86.png)

## next steps

CAD the other half and attachments! See you guys soon :D

### 2026-10-27: # Splitting, Slicing and Costs

**2h**

# Splitting, Slicing and Costs
## tl;dr
I split the back frame into two parts since the whole frame would be too big for most printers.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/061d21485f35691aae5f070816fa04b42bc7cfc5721cfd9034031883691d7cdd.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/52cf3eec38d2d6cfa42fa2b07d998330d7750ba88fdcadfea6c5e6ee3e228cfb.png)

## Slicing

While I was at it I downloaded a slicer to calculate the cost of the prints, which was needed in the BOM.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/b5d01f66e30ef496cf9c1066cf62918c8cf9a3fa1527ce3f363e9ef74cae3bb3.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/u4daV3AON4Vg7wKuOmDpozDubBrsNyfk/42376a4f320ec9e908f63cda3bc6ca82f81ab50667cbcd267d24a66c2cc24ee9.png)

As you can see the front frame is tilted to fit as well as provide space for some other parts, meaning you only need around 3-4 plates to print!
